metadata.description: Complete weapons system data: 178 weapons across all 12 categories
metadata.notes: All weapons extracted from actual compendium data. Includes full stats, special abilities, costs, and descriptions.

manufacturers.name: Dilithium
manufacturers.description: Melee weapons only. Dilithium blades with crystalline edges.

manufacturers.name: Monomolecular
manufacturers.description: Melee weapons only. Monomolecular blades with atom-thin edges.

weapons.name: Paralyzer Pistol
weapons.desc: The Paralyzer pistol is a nonlethal weapon designed to incapacitate rather than kill. It's an ideal choice for those who need to take down targets without causing permanent harm. With good range and impressive stopping power, the Paralyzer pistol can take down most targets with ease. Although it's nonlethal, it still packs a punch against anything other than heavy defenses. If you're looking for a weapon that can subdue your target without causing permanent damage, the Paralyzer pistol is the perfect choice.

weapons.name: Icer Pistol
weapons.desc: The Icer pistol is a lifesaving tool that is often packaged into medkits and emergency stations. It's a unique firearm that uses cold fusion technology to propel pellets of ice at deadly speed. Although the Icer pistol does low damage, it has unlimited ammo, making it the perfect weapon for emergency situations. The Icer pistol is a compact and lightweight firearm that can be used by anyone. It's easy to handle and the recoil is minimal. The pellets of ice can be deadly, piercing through skin and organs, causing frostbite and damage to internal organs. It's a weapon that's perfect for those who want to defend themselves in a pinch, or for those who need to hunt for food in extreme conditions. The Icer pistol is a unique and valuable tool that can make all the difference in a life-threatening situation.

weapons.name: Needler Pistol
weapons.desc: The Needler pistol is a generic weapon that has thousands of variations, but they all share one key feature: the ability to fire metal particles at extreme velocities, turning them into needles. This unique design gives the Needler pistol incredible stopping power, but its low penetration makes it unsuitable against heavily armored targets. The needles are deadly, causing massive tissue damage and leaving their targets in excruciating pain. With its high damage output, the Needler pistol is perfect for close-range combat, where its lack of penetration is not as much of an issue. The Needler pistol is a versatile weapon that can be used for a variety of purposes, from hunting to self-defense. With its generic design and high stopping power, the Needler pistol is a reliable and deadly firearm that should not be underestimated.

weapons.name: Laser Pistol
weapons.desc: The laser pistol is the ubiquitous weapon of choice for those who need a reliable and affordable firearm. With its generic design and thousands of variations, the laser pistol can be found just about everywhere, even in vending machines scattered throughout the galaxy. It's a low-end pistol that is easy to use, and easy to maintain. The laser pistol fires a beam of light that can slice through metal or flesh with ease. It's the perfect weapon for those who want to make a quick getaway or defend themselves in a tight spot. The laser pistol may not be the fanciest or most advanced weapon out there, but it gets the job done. Whether you're a mercenary, a smuggler, or just someone looking for a little extra protection, the laser pistol is a reliable companion that won't let you down.

weapons.name: Electron Pistol
weapons.desc: The Electron pistol is a generic design that was perfected during the Tronik war. Not only does it pack a serious punch, but it also has the ability to fry up any electronics it comes in contact with, making it an excellent choice for those who need to take down robots and drones. However, due to its archaic internals and rushed design, the Electron pistol is a difficult weapon to master. It requires significant training and skill to use accurately. But for those who put in the effort, the Electron pistol can be a devastating weapon in the right hands. If you're looking for a weapon that can take out both flesh and metal targets, look no further than the Electron pistol.

weapons.name: Plasma Pistol
weapons.desc: The Plasma Pistol is a powerful energy weapon that unleashes a stream of superheated plasma at close range. Its signature blue bolts strike with the force of a miniaturized sun, searing through flesh and armor with ease. Despite its fearsome reputation, the Plasma Pistol is a notoriously temperamental weapon that requires a steady hand and an intimate understanding of its unique internal workings. Its ability to reduce targets to smoldering piles of ash make it a favorite of those who seek to leave a lasting impression on their enemies.

weapons.name: Fragger Pistol
weapons.desc: The Fragger is a mean-looking pistol that packs a punch. It's a low-end weapon that was once a laser pistol, but it has been heavily modified on the streets. The result is a firearm that is deadly and unpredictable. The Fragger shoots bursts of plasma that tear through metal and flesh with ease. Some say that the Fragger has a mind of its own, and that it has a taste for violence. Whether you're a law enforcement officer or a street thug, the Fragger is a weapon that demands respect.

weapons.name: Gauss Needler Pistol
weapons.desc: The Gauss Needler pistol is an upgraded version of the standard Needler pistol, designed with improved internals that make it easier to use. It trades some range for improved damage and delivers deadly accuracy at close and medium ranges. Its high damage output and fast firing rate make it an ideal weapon for taking down targets quickly. If you're looking for a weapon that can deliver a serious punch and is easy to handle, the Gauss Needler pistol is the perfect choice.

weapons.name: Survivor Pistol
weapons.desc: The Laser Pistol Survival Edition is a rugged and reliable firearm that is designed to withstand the toughest conditions. With improved maintenance and an unlimited ammo capacity, it's the perfect weapon for those who need to survive in the harshest environments. The Survival pistol has a reinforced frame and a durable finish that resists rust and wear. The unlimited ammo capacity allows for long periods of use without the need to reload, and the weapon is designed for quick and easy maintenance in the field. The laser beam is powerful and accurate, with the added benefit of conserving ammo in the process. The Laser Pistol Survival Edition is the perfect weapon for those who need to defend themselves against the dangers of the wilderness or survive in a post-apocalyptic world. With its rugged design, enhanced capabilities, and reliable performance, the Laser Pistol Survival Edition is the ultimate survival weapon that won't let you down when you need it most.

weapons.name: Beretta XR-5 Pistol
weapons.desc: The Beretta XR-5 may be small and concealable, but it's not a weapon for the faint of heart. With its ultra-quiet operation and small size, the XR-5 is a challenging weapon to use with accuracy. The suppressor built into the barrel makes the recoil difficult to manage, and the small size of the weapon can make it challenging to aim. The laser sight helps to improve accuracy, but it still takes a steady hand to make every shot count. The XR-5 is not a weapon for beginners, and it takes a lot of practice to use it effectively. But for those who are up to the challenge, the XR-5 is the ultimate holdout pistol. Its small size and quiet operation make it perfect for covert operations or situations where stealth is critical. With the Beretta XR-5, you can take out your target with deadly precision, but you'll need to work for it.

weapons.name: Heavy Needler Pistol
weapons.desc: The Heavy Needler pistol is a weapon that was ahead of its time, but never saw much market adoption due to the rise of the Gauss Needler. It's an improved version of the Needler pistol, with better internals that make it easier to use and pack a more powerful punch. The Heavy Needler delivers serious damage to its targets, and its improved design means that it's faster and more accurate than its predecessor. Unlike the Gauss Needler, the Heavy Needler maintains its impressive range, making it a versatile weapon that can be used in a variety of combat situations. Despite its lack of popularity, the Heavy Needler remains a favorite among those who appreciate its reliability and superior firepower.

weapons.name: Defender Pistol
weapons.desc: The Defender pistol is a rare and highly sought-after variant of the standard Needler pistol. It boasts higher damage and more sophisticated internals, making it extremely quick and easy to use. The Defender's advanced targeting system ensures that its needles hit their mark with pinpoint accuracy, and its powerful propulsion system ensures that those needles deliver a devastating punch upon impact. This combination of power and precision makes the Defender pistol a force to be reckoned with on the battlefield. If you're lucky enough to get your hands on a Defender, you'll find that it's a weapon that's both deadly and easy to handle. Whether you're taking down enemies at close range or engaging them from a distance, the Defender pistol is a reliable choice that won't let you down.

weapons.name: Blaster Pistol
weapons.desc: The blaster pistol, a ubiquitous weapon found in the hands of security forces and civilians alike, is a jack-of-all-trades weapon that offers decent damage and accuracy at a relatively low cost. Despite its commonness, it's a reliable weapon that can get the job done in a pinch. However, its lack of unique features and limited customization options mean it's not the first choice for those looking for a weapon with personality.

weapons.name: Colt Predator Pistol
weapons.desc: The Colt Predator pistol is a true icon of the galaxy's underbelly, a weapon that's more about form than function. Its intimidating size and appearance make it a symbol of power and authority among the criminal underworld. The Colt Predator packs a serious punch, delivering devastating damage to its targets. However, its design is practically ancient, with clunky, outdated internals that result in high recoil and poor handling. The Colt Predator's real value lies in its aesthetic appeal, rather than its combat effectiveness. Its status as a symbol of intimidation and power is what makes it truly valuable to those who wield it. Despite its shortcomings, the Colt Predator remains a popular choice for those looking to make a statement, whether on the streets of a lawless planet or in the halls of a galactic crime syndicate.

weapons.name: Heavy Laser Pistol
weapons.desc: The Heavy Laser Pistol is a modified version of the standard laser pistol, designed for increased damage and range. It's a reliable weapon, but it comes at a steep price. Costing more than double the price of a standard laser pistol, it's not a great value for the increased performance. However, if you're looking for a weapon that packs a punch and can deliver deadly accuracy at long range, the Heavy Laser Pistol is worth considering.

weapons.name: Mass Pistol
weapons.desc: The Mass Pistol is a rare find in the galaxy, with only a select few able to get their hands on one. Despite its compact size, the heavy pistol packs a powerful punch, capable of stopping even the most formidable foes in their tracks. However, the Mass Pistol's range leaves much to be desired, making it unsuitable for long-range engagements. Its limited availability only adds to its allure, making it a highly coveted weapon among those in the know.

weapons.name: Excal Blaster
weapons.desc: The Excal Blaster pistol is a rare and coveted weapon that has been modified to include armor piercing capabilities, making it a powerful tool for those who need to penetrate even the toughest defenses. While it sacrifices a bit of damage and ammo capacity to achieve this, its armor-piercing capabilities make it a top choice for those who face heavily armored opponents.

weapons.name: Equaliser Pistol
weapons.desc: The Equaliser pistol is a rare energy weapon that's fast, powerful, and regarded as an excellent choice for close combat. However, its poor range and finicky nature make it difficult to use effectively. Owning an Equaliser pistol requires practice and skill to master. But for those who put in the time and effort, it can be a deadly weapon. Its rarity and reputation make it a prized possession for those lucky enough to own one. If you're willing to put in the practice.

weapons.name: Skalan Grudge
weapons.desc: The Skalan Grudge pistol is a weapon feared across the galaxy, renowned for its sheer power, size and weight. Almost exclusively used by the Skalan Order, this pistol is not for the faint of heart. Its heavy frame and 3-round magazine make it a challenge to wield, and only the toughest marksmen can handle it without injuring themselves. But for those who can, each shot packs an incredible punch, making even the hardiest of foes think twice before crossing paths with anyone wielding the Grudge.

weapons.name: Photon Pistol
weapons.desc: The Photon Pistol, a prized and rare weapon, is sought after by those who value its power and versatility. Despite its restricted legality, this excellent all-around pistol is revered for its reliability and effectiveness. In the hands of a skilled user, the Photon Pistol is a true force to be reckoned with.

weapons.name: Disintegrator Pistol
weapons.desc: The Disintegrator Pistol is a medium-powered energy weapon designed to penetrate force fields, making it a highly sought after and restricted weapon in the galaxy. Its limited availability only adds to its desirability among those who are willing to break the law to get their hands on it. The weapon's unique technology allows it to penetrate even the most advanced force fields, making it a formidable tool in the hands of a skilled user.

weapons.name: Tachyon Pistol
weapons.desc: The Tachyon Pistol is the perfect weapon for any assassin or criminal seeking to carry out a job discreetly. It makes no sound, no light, and leaves no traces, making it nearly impossible to detect. With its excellent range and rare availability, the Tachyon Pistol is a highly sought after tool of the trade. However, mastering this weapon is no easy feat. It takes years of dedicated practice to wield it effectively.

weapons.name: Gama Pistol
weapons.desc: The Gama Pistol is a marvel of high-tech engineering, boasting exceptional damage, impressive range, and unmatched usability. A capable wielder can turn this weapon into a true force to be reckoned with. Unfortunately, due to its extremely limited production, the Gama Pistol is a rare sight in the galaxy.

weapons.name: X-Laser Pistol
weapons.desc: The X-Laser pistol is the sidearm of choice for elite military operatives across the galaxy. Its advanced technology allows this weapon to fire shots that are almost invisible, while still delivering the power, range, and damage that seasoned veterans demand. The manufacturing process for the X-Laser is involved and expensive, resulting in very few units being available on the market. If you can get your hands on one, the X-Laser will give you an edge in any firefight.

weapons.name: B39 Laser Pistol
weapons.desc: The B39 Laser Pistol is a top-secret design favored by covert operatives for its compact size and immense power. The details of its technology are shrouded in secrecy, but what is known is that the B39 is capable of delivering a massive amount of energy in a very small package. The weapon is perfect for quick and efficient assassinations where a compact, yet devastating weapon is necessary. The B39 Laser Pistol is a prized possession of the most elite operatives, and very few are rumored to exist.

weapons.name: Fusion Pistol
weapons.desc: The Fusion Pistol is a weapon shrouded in mystery and rumors. It's rumored to be the ultimate weapon of its class, surpassing any other firearm in existence. Though it's classified and its very existence is often denied, whispers of a few prototypes existing have persisted throughout the galaxy. According to the rumors, the Fusion Pistol is capable of piercing through even the toughest of armor with ease, and its shooting capabilities are unparalleled. The few who are aware of its existence believe that it could change the face of warfare if it were to ever become widely available.

weapons.name: Hunting Rifle
weapons.desc: A civilian rifle built for people who want one tool that never turns into a project. It is commonly sold with optional variants and accessories because the galaxy cannot leave well enough alone. Reliable, simple, and still seen in the hands of hunters who do not trust anything that needs a technician on standby.

weapons.name: Laser Rifle
weapons.desc: A clean, popular platform that scales up the laser sidearm philosophy into a primary weapon. Burst capability makes it feel professional without becoming demanding, and the huge number of available configurations ensures two owners rarely carry the same version. It is boring in the best possible way.

weapons.name: Electron Rifle
weapons.desc: A rifle that exists for targets with circuitry, not courage. It is the kind of weapon that makes drones look like scrap and turns powered gear into expensive dead weight. When someone brings one, the smart machines stop feeling smart.

weapons.name: KR 80 Mass Rifle
weapons.desc: A low-end mass rifle that still insists on making impact a physical event. Explosive payloads mean placement matters less than proximity, and it is often chosen by people who prefer certainty over finesse. It is common enough to be familiar, and loud enough to be remembered.

weapons.name: RV-10 Frontier Rifle
weapons.desc: A fast, practical frontier rifle that favors movement and quick follow-through. It is often sold in modular variants because frontier owners love to turn one rifle into three different solutions. Think of it as the rifle equivalent of a multitool that somebody kept upgrading until it became sharp.

weapons.name: Gauss Needler Rifle
weapons.desc: Needler tech in rifle form, tuned for speed and repeatability. Burst and full-auto capability make it a common favorite for people who want volume without losing control, and the needle profile tends to find vulnerable seams more often than opponents would like. It is popular for the same reason it keeps showing up. It works.

weapons.name: KR 8000 Mass Rifle
weapons.desc: The KR 8000 takes the mass rifle concept and adds a heavy dose of commitment. Explosive payloads at this scale tend to rearrange environments, which makes it less a “rifle” and more a portable policy change. Rare, expensive, and usually acquired through someone who insists it was an “opportunity.”

weapons.name: Gauss Battle Rifle
weapons.desc: A needler platform built for sustained engagements and well-funded users. Full-auto capability plus a large magazine make it a battlefield workhorse, and the option ecosystem means units often field their own signature variants. It is less a personal weapon and more a program.

weapons.name: Plasma Rifle
weapons.desc: A rifle that keeps doing its job after the shot lands. Ongoing burn makes it excellent for forcing movement and punishing anyone who thought cover would solve the problem. People who favor it tend to prefer outcomes that continue even when attention shifts elsewhere.

weapons.name: Paralyzer Rifle
weapons.desc: A nonlethal rifle for professionals who want compliance at distance. Quick handling and widespread configurable variants make it a favorite for security teams, bounty crews, and anyone who wants the target alive and annoyed. Its restricted status mostly means the paperwork is thicker than the barrel.

weapons.name: Gamatox Rifle
weapons.desc: A rifle engineered around the idea that defenses are negotiable. It is built to break through protection and make the target feel suddenly underdressed, even when they are not. Users tend to be practical people who dislike long engagements.

weapons.name: Blaster Rifle
weapons.desc: A dependable energy rifle with minimal personality and a strong record of showing up when needed. It is the sort of weapon that ends up in armories because nobody regrets issuing it. Reliable, functional, and often the first rifle someone learns to trust.

weapons.name: Akama 120 Rifle
weapons.desc: A pre-modern design that survived into the future by refusing to rely on modern assumptions. It shrugs off electronic interference because there is barely any electronics to interfere with, and it remains popular because it keeps firing under conditions that embarrass newer rifles. Owners tend to speak about it the way mechanics speak about old engines. With respect and a small grin.

weapons.name: Screamer Rifle
weapons.desc: A spiritual rifle that behaves like it was designed to annoy forcefields specifically. It is a strange piece of kit that makes shielded targets reconsider their comfort, and its scarcity keeps it more rumor than inventory. People who claim to have used one rarely agree on the details, which is convenient.

weapons.name: Multi-Load Smart Rifle
weapons.desc: A flexible rifle designed around quick role changes rather than single-purpose obsession. Modular variants are common, and owners tend to tune it for whatever they expect to face next, sometimes during the same job. It has the reputation of a rifle that always has a plan, even if the user does not.

weapons.name: Mass Accelerator Rifle
weapons.desc: A rifle for people who like precision but do not require politeness. Explosive payloads reduce the importance of perfect placement, and critical spikes turn good hits into very bad outcomes for the target. It is rare enough to feel like a statement even before the first shot.

weapons.name: Disintegrator Rifle
weapons.desc: A deliberate, high-end rifle with a particular talent for making forcefields feel less reassuring. Its limited presence in the market keeps it spoken about more than it is seen, and most sightings come with contradictory details. That is often what “limited” really means.

weapons.name: Photon E-Rifle
weapons.desc: A rifle built to punish electronics and anything dependent on them. It is commonly configured with different operational packages, and the users who seek it out tend to have very specific enemies in mind. Limited availability ensures most people only meet it from the wrong side.

weapons.name: Super-X Rifle
weapons.desc: A discreet penetration-focused rifle that favors operators who prefer to remain unremarkable while producing remarkable outcomes. It is the kind of platform that turns defenses into a temporary inconvenience, then disappears back into the environment. Limited distribution keeps it expensive and quietly desirable.

weapons.name: Rage Repeater Rifle
weapons.desc: A rifle that turns recoil management into a skill test. Full-auto capability exists here as a challenge as much as a feature, and the weapon repays discipline with brutal throughput. Its illegal status has done little to reduce its popularity in places where survival matters more than compliance.

weapons.name: Splatter Riffle
weapons.desc: A high-power rifle designed for direct, physical authority. Armor interaction improves as defenses climb, and recoil ensures the user participates in the experience. It is rare, illegal, and favored by people built like they expect to win wrestling matches against machinery.

weapons.name: Photon Rifle
weapons.desc: A rifle tuned for electronic targets, built around shutting machines down hard and fast. Full-auto capability turns it into a problem for drones, networks, and anyone relying on automated protection. Illegal and limited, it tends to circulate through hands that already have a reason to avoid receipts.

weapons.name: Scythe Rifle
weapons.desc: A high-power rifle that shows up mostly as a whispered line item. It performs like a professional tool with no interest in marketing, and its classified status ensures details stay conveniently inconsistent. People who claim to have one usually change the subject soon after.

weapons.name: Meson Rifle
weapons.desc: A classified weapon that exists in the space between “prototype” and “myth.” Reports describe high power and uncomfortable effectiveness, but the specifics never line up across sources. That is often how you can tell the classification is working.

weapons.name: Fusion Rifle
weapons.desc: A classified rifle built to make heavy armor feel like a bad investment. It is one of those weapons that has more stories than confirmed owners, and those stories never agree on where it came from. The few consistent details are the ones that matter.

weapons.name: Barret 180 Sniper
weapons.desc: The Barret 180 remains the longrange benchmark. It is configurable, reliable, and candid about recoil. Its continued presence in serious loadouts has less to do with nostalgia than with results.

weapons.name: Urban Recon III Sniper
weapons.desc: The Urban Recon III is built for environments that resist traditional sniper doctrine. Compact dimensions and quiet operation allow it to function without anchoring the user in place. It is favored where relocation is expected, not optional.

weapons.name: Tachyonic Sniper
weapons.desc: The Tachyonic Sniper produces results without residue. No signature, no trace, and no easy reconstruction. Its demands on the user are substantial, and the outcomes reflect that investment.

weapons.name: Antimatter Sniper
weapons.desc: The Antimatter Sniper operates beyond conventional engagement assumptions. Impact effects extend past the target, and survivability becomes a secondary concern. The engineering resolves precision before the user ever arrives.

weapons.name: Barret 430 XXL Sniper
weapons.desc: The 430 XXL emphasizes certainty over refinement. Heavy ammunition and severe recoil define its operation, and setup is nonnegotiable. Its results are straightforward to assess.

weapons.name: Gugnir Anti Material Sniper
weapons.desc: The Gugnir was built for targets that were never meant to recover. Extended reach and sustained engagement capability eliminate the need for followup. Antimaterial is not a descriptor. It is a boundary condition.

weapons.name: Orbital Sledgehammer Sniper
weapons.desc: The Orbital Sledgehammer fires infrequently and resets slowly, which is appropriate given its effects. Impact sites become landmarks rather than objectives, and reports vary widely depending on proximity. The classification remains intact.

weapons.name: Needler SMG
weapons.desc: A compact needler platform made for close-range tempo. Modular variants are common, and the needle system has a habit of finding vulnerable points more often than opponents would like. It is legal, common, and frequently underestimated by people who have not read medical reports.

weapons.name: Laser SMG
weapons.desc: A fast-handling energy SMG designed to stay mobile. It is commonly sold in multiple configurations, which is appropriate because it ends up everywhere. People buy it because it keeps up and keeps working.

weapons.name: Needler SR-1 SMG
weapons.desc: A tighter, more disciplined needler SMG that favors control over volume. It is a common choice for users who treat ammunition like a resource rather than a suggestion. It feels less like spraying and more like stitching.

weapons.name: Urban Watch II SMG
weapons.desc: An institutional compact weapon, sold in many approved configurations and built to behave predictably in dense environments. It is the sort of SMG that ends up standardized because nobody wants surprises in hallways and stairwells. It is not glamorous. It is everywhere.

weapons.name: Gauss Needler MX2 SMG
weapons.desc: A rare, upgraded needler SMG with a reputation for being more capable than its size suggests. It sits above most standard SMGs in performance, and below them in availability, which is how it became desirable. Owners tend to treat it like a personal favorite rather than a tool.

weapons.name: Evelith SMG
weapons.desc: A restricted compact platform that is popular precisely because it is so configurable. It performs well enough that somebody eventually decided it should not be as easy to acquire as it used to be. The people who already own one have not been persuaded to give it up.

weapons.name: Frontier Savage SMG
weapons.desc: A stubborn, old-tech SMG that refuses to care about electronic warfare. It kicks hard, works anyway, and is favored in places where power grids fail and people still insist on fighting. Illegal in polite jurisdictions, cherished everywhere else.

weapons.name: Photon SMG
weapons.desc: A limited, illegal SMG built around piercing defenses that other compact weapons bounce off. It exists for operators who expect sophisticated protection and refuse to accept “too small” as an excuse. Short ownership chains are common, usually because the owners keep moving.

weapons.name: Ripper Mini SMG
weapons.desc: A compact platform designed for people who need one hand free and still want meaningful output. It favors speed and opportunistic timing, and its illegal status fits the clientele. The magazine capacity suggests the designer expected the user to multitask under stress.

weapons.name: SMX 800 SMG
weapons.desc: A classified SMG that appears mostly as secondhand description and incomplete footage. The consistent theme is electronics failing quickly and witnesses arguing about what they actually saw. That level of uncertainty is either bad reporting or excellent classification.

weapons.name: Fusion SMG
weapons.desc: A high-power compact weapon built to humiliate heavy armor. Details are scarce, ownership stories are contradictory, and anyone claiming confirmed access tends to stop talking when pressed. In a catalogue full of illegal weapons, this one feels like a rumor with recoil.

weapons.name: Hunting Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Hunting Shotgun is a solved problem that refuses to become obsolete. It functions exactly where it is supposed to, tolerates endless modification, and continues to appear wherever people value reliability over novelty. Entire industries exist to replace it. None have succeeded.

weapons.name: MX-MK2 "Acupuncturer" Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Acupuncturer is optimized for encounters that collapse quickly. Its effective space is small, its handling is immediate, and its use favors initiative over intimidation. It is carried by people who do not expect a second exchange.

weapons.name: Blaster Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Blaster Shotgun replaces ritual with consistency. Energy cycling removes the usual maintenance concerns without changing the expected outcome at close range. It appeals to users who want the effect of a shotgun without the personality that often comes with one.

weapons.name: Defender Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Defender treats armor as a variable rather than a defense. Capacity and accuracy are preserved where other designs compromise, and the platform remains stable under repeated use. Ownership tends to be permanent.

weapons.name: M.E.G 306 "Pepperbox" Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Pepperbox was designed for controlled interior use and issued accordingly. Burst capability exists to resolve situations quickly without inviting excess, and the reload process enforces pacing whether the user intends it or not. Its continued adoption is procedural, not sentimental.

weapons.name: Pulse Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Pulse Shotgun delivers output that demands restraint. Residual energy and heat accumulation mean poor timing is immediately punished. Effective use depends on forethought rather than aggression.

weapons.name: Tachyonic Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Tachyonic Shotgun leaves no obvious trace of its operation. Its value lies in what remains unexplained afterward rather than what occurs in the moment. It favors precision over spectacle.

weapons.name: Combat Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Combat Shotgun pushes the platform into sustained automatic fire, with consequences that escalate rapidly. Control is learned through experience, not assumed by design. Its scarcity reflects how few users consider this a reasonable tradeoff.

weapons.name: Emissary Gravity Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Emissary prioritizes force distribution over discrimination. Structural damage is expected, not incidental, and prolonged use is discouraged by the weapon itself. It is deployed where the environment has already been written off.

weapons.name: Scatterbrain Shotgun
weapons.desc: The Scatterbrain demands setup. Size, weight, and bracing limit when it can be brought to bear, not what it does once deployed. When conditions are met, it justifies every constraint imposed by its design.

weapons.name: FL-44 Apocalypse Shotgun
weapons.desc: The FL44 exists at the edge of categorization. Braced operation, extreme reach, and overwhelming output coexist without apology. Most encounters with it occur only as reference points.

weapons.name: Malik GV-20 Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The GV-20 is the workhorse people graduate into. It does sustained fire without attitude and accepts enough modification to stay relevant across campaigns. It is the kind of gun that ends up with stickers on it, not because it is cool, but because it stays.

weapons.name: Malik GV-35 Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The GV-35 is what happens when the GV-20 gets refined by veterans with long memories. Better control, longer endurance, fewer reasons to pause. It feels less like wrestling and more like operating a tool that was built with human anatomy in mind.

weapons.name: Gauss HCR Auto Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The HCR Auto is a machine gun that behaves like it was trained. It places rounds with intention at rates that should make intention impossible, and the cumulative effect is quietly brutal. It is favored by people who want volume without waste.

weapons.name: Hakari D.I.N.O Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The D.I.N.O is Hakari practicality wearing a bad mood. Built from spare ship components and whatever else Mangara had lying around, it was designed to keep firing in conditions where smarter weapons stop cooperating. It exists for a specific enemy and a specific kind of war, and it carries that history in every ugly, stubborn part.

weapons.name: Calshan MK-V Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The MK-V is for targets who trusted their protection too much. It is blunt in purpose and expensive in consequence, the sort of weapon that makes procurement officers nervous and operators satisfied. If you see one in the field, somebody planned for armor.

weapons.name: Crusader Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The Crusader is braced for a reason. It exists to drown electronics in disruption until drones drop, systems fail, and powered hardware turns into dead weight. Against the wrong opponent it looks unfair. Against the right opponent it looks necessary.

weapons.name: Micropulse Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The Micropulse is what you issue when force fields are common enough to be annoying. It keeps applying pressure in the one place the defense hoped you could not. The recoil is significant, but it is mostly a reminder that physics is still part of the contract.

weapons.name: Calshan MK-IX Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The MK-IX is not an upgrade, it is escalation. It takes the MK-V’s intent and adds enough power and control to make sustained fire feel almost procedural. Bracing is assumed. So is the fact that this was not meant to be widely owned.

weapons.name: Skalan Boomer
weapons.desc: The Skalan Boomer was built for people shaped like walking fortifications. It is oversized, violent, and tuned for operators whose bones treat recoil as background noise. In anyone else’s hands it is a medical emergency with a trigger.

weapons.name: Skalan Slugger Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The Slugger is the Boomer after someone decided that hitting the right thing mattered more than hitting everything. Still oversized, still Skalander-built, still completely indifferent to human ergonomics. It is control for a species that considers excess a baseline.

weapons.name: Fusion Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The Fusion Machine Gun is rarely described in specifics, mostly because few descriptions come from anyone who saw it from the right side. The sources disagree on details and agree on outcomes. It is the kind of hardware that leaves only one question afterward: who had access to it.

weapons.name: Anti Riot Launcher
weapons.desc: The Anti Riot Launcher delivers crowd dispersal with the minimum force required to make the point. Official documentation emphasizes nonlethal outcomes. The crowd usually disagrees.

weapons.name: A.R.L Cloud Launcher
weapons.desc: The Cloud Launcher deploys persistent area denial with enough volume to make retreat the correct choice. Fullauto capability ensures coverage rather than precision. Its presence signals preparation rather than escalation.

weapons.name: Wrist Launcher
weapons.desc: The Wrist Launcher puts explosive force where ergonomics say it should not fit. Fast operation and interruption capability make it useful in close engagements. The logistics are left to the user.

weapons.name: Pulse Launcher
weapons.desc: The Pulse Launcher rewards restraint. One shot, measured radius, and a recharge that keeps pace with careful movement. It is favored by operators who treat explosives as tools rather than statements.

weapons.name: Cluster Mortar Launcher
weapons.desc: The Cluster Mortar treats accuracy as optional. Coverage is the goal, and the radius ensures it. Six rounds and a complex reload make it unsuitable for improvisation, which is exactly why it exists.

weapons.name: Biotox Launcher
weapons.desc: The Biotox Launcher deploys a gas that persists and continues causing biological harm. The launcher itself remains technically legal. The payload does not. This distinction rarely survives debrief.

weapons.name: Disposable Launcher
weapons.desc: The Disposable Launcher fires once and is discarded. Simple, legal, and brutally honest about its role, it is purchased in bulk by anyone who expects to need more than one.

weapons.name: V-15 Infantry Launcher
weapons.desc: The V15 carries heavy ordnance with defensepiercing capability and asks nothing of the operator beyond pointing it correctly. Skill was replaced by engineering long before the trigger was pulled.

weapons.name: Armageddon Gatling Launcher
weapons.desc: The Armageddon Gatling fires explosive rounds at fullauto rates. The name explains itself. Armor becomes a budget issue rather than a tactical one.

weapons.name: Hunter Missile Launcher
weapons.desc: The Hunter locks on and commits fully. Single use, braced operation, and ten meters of consequence at impact. Guidance rewards experience, but it rarely needs help finding its target.

weapons.name: Hellfire Launcher
weapons.desc: The Hellfire is assigned, not purchased. Six shots, wide blast, and classified documentation describe a weapon intended for moments when escalation has already been approved. Atmospheric reports afterward remain restricted.

weapons.name: Auto-Missile System
weapons.desc: The AutoMissile System engages targets at distances where direct combat becomes theoretical. Guidance manages tracking. Blast radius manages error. Planning matters more than reflex.

weapons.name: Victimizer Howitzer Canon
weapons.desc: The Victimizer is a handheld siege platform. Bracing is required to survive its use. The name was applied after the first deployment by someone who watched it work.

weapons.name: EMP Shockwave Canon
weapons.desc: The EMP Shockwave Cannon delivers electronic denial across a wide radius with enough force to make redundancy meaningless. Against networked defenses, it is conclusive.

weapons.name: Titan Canon
weapons.desc: The Titan Cannon fires once per scene. This fact alone explains everything else. Three shots are usually sufficient.

weapons.name: Point defense canon
weapons.desc: The Point Defense Cannon exists to ensure incoming threats do not arrive. Fullauto tracking and extreme range make interception routine rather than dramatic. Common for installations that expect trouble.

weapons.name: Light Laser canon
weapons.desc: The Light Laser Cannon is the entry point for shipscale combat. Burst capable, predictable recharge, and respectable range. It fills the role competently without ambition.

weapons.name: Mass Driver Canon
weapons.desc: The Mass Driver applies physics directly. Defensepiercing ordnance at extreme range answers most questions immediately. At this scale, burst fire becomes unnecessary.

weapons.name: Photon Canon
weapons.desc: The Photon Cannon delivers sustained energy fire at ranges that exceed personalscale comprehension. Armor interaction is resolved differently at this level. Its presence usually defines the engagement.

weapons.name: Excel Shreder Canon
weapons.desc: The Excel Shredder fires armorrending rounds that cause structural damage on contact. At ship scale, that result produces very quick responses from everything nearby.

weapons.name: Pulse Laser Canon
weapons.desc: The Pulse Laser Cannon treats range as preference rather than limitation. Fast recharge, defensepiercing output, and fullauto capability make it decisive early.

weapons.name: Sogar Canon
weapons.desc: The Sogar applies force damage across a wide burst radius. At fleet scale, that makes it crowd control rather than precision fire. It is used where denial matters more than destruction.

weapons.name: Heavy Pulsar Canon
weapons.desc: The Heavy Pulsar occupies significant tonnage and repays it by making cover negotiable. Fifty meters of force damage answers most tactical concerns.

weapons.name: Plasma Canon
weapons.desc: The Plasma Cannon fires superheated ordnance that occasionally creates secondary problems if mishandled. The HOT warning is both technical note and survival advice.

weapons.name: Combat Laser Canon
weapons.desc: The Combat Laser Cannon defines outcomes before opponents realize an engagement has begun. Large magazine, fullauto capability, and extreme range make it unforgiving.

weapons.name: Photon Disruptor Canon
weapons.desc: The Photon Disruptor combines defense penetration, armor rending, and electronic disruption in one platform. At this scale, specialization becomes redundancy.

weapons.name: Pulse Defender MK2 Canon
weapons.desc: The Pulse Defender MK2 stacks critical capability, EMP, and defense piercing into a rapidfire platform. It exists because layered defenses became common.

weapons.name: Antimater Canon
weapons.desc: The Antimatter Cannon fires at extreme power across a blast radius measured in tens of thousands of meters. Production is limited for reasons no one disputes. Auditors ask questions anyway.

weapons.name: Longbow Magrail Canon
weapons.desc: The Longbow fires physical ordnance at ranges measured in millions of meters. Defensepiercing output at that distance turns infrastructure into a temporary concept.

weapons.name: Kraven Laser Canon
weapons.desc: The Kraven Laser Cannon exceeds known design expectations. Its origin is disputed. Its performance is not. Armor becomes irrelevant very quickly.

weapons.name: Nova Canon
weapons.desc: The Nova Cannon delivers effects measured in tenmillionmeter increments. Recharge cycles are counted in scenes rather than rounds. Staffing requirements are omitted from catalogues for brevity.

weapons.name: Smoke Grenade
weapons.desc: The Smoke Grenade removes visibility without escalating consequences. It is cheap, legal, and carried by anyone who has learned that not being seen is often more effective than being armed. The cloud does not discriminate. Planning does.

weapons.name: Molotov
weapons.desc: The Molotov is improvised fire made portable. Cheap, legal, and universally understood, it persists because the underlying physics have never stopped working. It does not require training. It requires intent.

weapons.name: Glitter field Grenade
weapons.desc: The Glitter Field Grenade understates itself by name. Within its area, energy weapons lose their authority and damage becomes disappointing by design. The effect is temporary. The frustration it causes tends to linger.

weapons.name: Demolex Bomb
weapons.desc: The Demolex is placed, not thrown, and that distinction matters. It exists for structural problems where timing and precision matter more than spectacle. People who use it tend to arrive early and leave calmly.

weapons.name: Stun Grenade
weapons.desc: The Stun Grenade exists where force is required but permanence is not. It overwhelms senses long enough to establish control and then steps back. Security forces rely on it because it ends resistance without creating aftermath.

weapons.name: Fragmentation Grenade
weapons.desc: The Fragmentation Grenade is the default answer that never needed improvement. Medium power, predictable radius, and immediate effect. It has remained unchanged because nothing about it needed fixing.

weapons.name: Plasma Grenade
weapons.desc: The Plasma Grenade makes an area hostile even after the detonation finishes. Energy damage continues to assert itself, discouraging return and complicating pursuit. People who have seen one used tend to remember where they were standing.

weapons.name: Shock Grenade
weapons.desc: The Shock Grenade exists for electronics and everything that depends on them. Drones drop. Systems fail. Powered equipment becomes expensive debris. Against biological targets it is unpleasant. Against machines it is final.

weapons.name: Ripper Grenade
weapons.desc: The Ripper Grenade focuses less on damage and more on negation. Armor becomes an unreliable investment once the shrapnel arrives. It is small, rare, and chosen specifically for targets who trusted their protection too much.

weapons.name: Phantasmal Grenade
weapons.desc: The Phantasmal Grenade covers a wide area with ongoing physical harm delivered by means few reports agree on. What matters is persistence. Whatever enters the cloud does not leave unchanged.

weapons.name: Death Gas Grenade
weapons.desc: The Death Gas Grenade is named with unusual honesty. It targets living tissue specifically and continues working after deployment. Regulatory distinctions do not survive contact with its effects.

weapons.name: Cluster Grenade
weapons.desc: The Cluster Grenade turns a small throw into a wide problem. Submunitions saturate the area well beyond what the size suggests. The illegal status exists because someone did the math.

weapons.name: EMP Bomb
weapons.desc: The EMP Bomb ends electronic activity across a wide area without damaging the infrastructure itself. Everything dependent on power becomes irrelevant at once. Recovery depends on replacement, not repair.

weapons.name: Neutron Bomb
weapons.desc: The Neutron Bomb is banned everywhere for reasons that do not require elaboration. Its effects are precise in a way that makes the intent impossible to ignore. Ownership implies an organization willing to accept that implication.

weapons.name: C12 Bomb
weapons.desc: The C12 is a placement tool for largescale outcomes. Fifty meters of effect means positioning matters long before detonation. It is rare, controlled, and deployed only when the justification has already been written.

weapons.name: Fusion Bomb
weapons.desc: The Fusion Bomb removes armor from consideration entirely. Engineering answered the skill question before the user arrived. What remains afterward tends to require documentation.

weapons.name: Grenade Attachment
weapons.desc: The Grenade Attachment takes a weapon that was already dangerous and adds flexibility. Three shots, quick use, and compatibility make it attractive to professionals who prefer contingencies built in rather than carried separately.

weapons.name: Grenade Launcher
weapons.desc: The Grenade Launcher is for operators who decided explosives were the plan, not the backup. Nine rounds and deliberate reloads reward foresight. It is legal, uncommon, and rarely misunderstood.

weapons.name: Unarmed
weapons.desc: Unarmed combat is the only weapon you cannot drop, lose, or have confiscated at a checkpoint. It scales entirely with commitment and timing, which means it looks harmless right up until it stops being. It will not solve every problem, but it solves more of them than polite society likes to admit.

weapons.name: Deathball Bat
weapons.desc: The Deathball Bat is sporting equipment the galaxy failed to keep in the sports section. It is sturdy, easy to use, and brutally effective even in the hands of someone who has never trained a day in their life. The fact that it comes in countless “collector” variants does not make it less practical. It makes it easier to justify owning three.

weapons.name: Nightstick
weapons.desc: The Nightstick is the universal symbol of compliance delivered at arm’s length. Compact, quick, and designed to control without escalating into permanent consequences, it is as much a tool of posture as it is impact. Skilled use looks boring. That is the point.

weapons.name: Claws
weapons.desc: Claws are not one weapon, they are an entire category wearing one name. Some are natural, some are manufactured, and some are both, built into hands that already had the idea. Predators use them because evolution worked. People use them because aftermarket catalogues did. Either way, the technique is the same and the result is rarely subtle.

weapons.name: Saber
weapons.desc: The Saber is what happens when balance becomes a threat. Light in the hand, fast on the line, and deceptively dangerous in practiced motion, it rewards confidence and punishes hesitation. It is popular for the same reason it has always been popular. It works, and it looks like it knows it.

weapons.name: Combat Knife
weapons.desc: The Combat Knife is the quiet constant. It fits anywhere, travels anywhere, and remains useful when everything else becomes awkward or unavailable. It does not need spectacle to be effective. It needs proximity and intent.

weapons.name: Hakari Karvik
weapons.desc: The Karvik carries tradition like weight and uses it like leverage. It is large, angular, and designed to press advantage through form rather than flourish. People who recognize it tend to react differently than people who do not, which is one of its less discussed features.

weapons.name: Staff
weapons.desc: The Staff is a geometry lesson delivered at speed. It controls distance, sets tempo, and offers nonlethal outcomes without being delicate about it. Entire martial lineages exist because this weapon never stopped being correct.

weapons.name: Mace
weapons.desc: The Mace is the anti-fashion of melee. It does not care what the target invested in, and it does not require the user to be clever. It hits, it breaks, and it moves on. If you want finesse, pick a different tool.

weapons.name: Spear
weapons.desc: The Spear is reach, penetration, and simplicity aligned into one idea. It keeps threats outside comfortable distance and still finds the weak point when distance fails. The galaxy has invented a lot of weapons since the spear. The spear has remained relevant through spite and physics.

weapons.name: Short Sword
weapons.desc: The Short Sword is built for gaps, corners, and close work. It is fast enough to exploit openings and practical enough to stay useful when the fight becomes cramped. People who choose it tend to dislike theatrics and enjoy endings.

weapons.name: War Maul
weapons.desc: The War Maul is a demolition tool that happened to become a weapon. It is heavy, exhausting, and brutally final when it lands. The only built-in limitation is what it does to the user’s stamina. Everyone else gets no such mercy.

weapons.name: Great sword
weapons.desc: The Great Sword is a commitment measured in muscle memory. It rewards dedication with terrifying efficiency, turning decisive moments into irreversible outcomes. Most people try it once. The few who stay with it become the reason it has never gone out of style.

weapons.name: Katana
weapons.desc: The Katana is a precision instrument disguised as a blade. It rewards discipline, timing, and mastery to a degree that feels unfair to anyone watching. The technique looks elegant. The results do not.

weapons.name: Glaive
weapons.desc: The Glaive is distance and authority in one silhouette. It keeps opponents where you want them, then punishes them for being there. In skilled hands it becomes less a weapon and more a moving boundary line.

weapons.name: Kusarigama
weapons.desc: The Kusarigama is a long-term project, not a purchase. It offers control from multiple angles, demands constant attention, and punishes sloppy movement immediately. Nobody “tries” this weapon. They either study it or they regret touching it.

weapons.name: Hakari Cetus
weapons.desc: The Cetus does not stop working when the strike ends. It leaves something behind that keeps doing its job, turning time into a resource the opponent no longer owns. In a prolonged fight, it changes the math without raising its voice.

weapons.name: Stun Baton
weapons.desc: The Stun Baton is institutional pragmatism made handheld. It is rechargeable, reliable, and designed to end resistance without creating paperwork that lasts forever. Security forces love it because it works the same way every time.

weapons.name: Searing Blade
weapons.desc: The Searing Blade turns a clean hit into a lingering problem. Even when armor takes the strike, the heat tends to follow through, finding seams and weaknesses the edge did not. The fight may end quickly. The aftermath does not.

weapons.name: Shock Saber
weapons.desc: The Shock Saber is for targets whose bodies contain wiring, servos, or expensive upgrades. Contact triggers a cascade of disruption that turns strength into stuttering failure. Against the wrong opponent, it feels less like a sword and more like pulling a plug.

weapons.name: Shock Mace
weapons.desc: The Shock Mace is consistent in the way a blunt instrument should be. It delivers steady powered damage without drama, without flair, and without needing ideal conditions. It is popular with people who value predictability over style.

weapons.name: Jaulaus Noogie Hammer
weapons.desc: The Noogie Hammer is a Jaulaus greeting translated into engineering. The blast is not politely directional and the wielder is in the radius, which Jaulaus consider acceptable because Jaulaus recover and most other species do not. The weapon is enormous, explosive, and culturally sincere in a way that should make you nervous.

weapons.name: Gravity Maul
weapons.desc: The Gravity Maul compresses the world for a moment and expects the world to cope. Electronics stutter, bodies buckle, and anything fragile learns a new definition of fragile. It does not require finesse. It requires space and follow-through.

weapons.name: Laser Sword
weapons.desc: The Laser Sword is speed paired with penetration. It is small enough to stay mobile and sharp enough to ignore protection that would stop other blades. It favors fighters who treat movement as offense.

weapons.name: Combat Blade
weapons.desc: The Combat Blade is oversized, powered, and rarely seen outside situations where rules have already stopped being relevant. People describe it in vague terms, which is usually a sign that the owner prefers it that way. If you have seen one clearly, it was already too close.

weapons.name: Chain Ripper
weapons.desc: The Chain Ripper is sustained contact turned into a weapon design philosophy. It distributes damage across multiple points and keeps doing it as long as it stays in motion. The sound is unforgettable. The clean-up is worse.

weapons.name: Omega Great blade
weapons.desc: The Omega Great Blade is spoken about more often than it is documented. The details vary by source, which is convenient for whoever keeps it that way. What remains consistent is this: when it appears, the pace of the fight changes immediately.

weapons.name: Nanotech Bioknife
weapons.desc: The Nanotech Bioknife exists mostly as a rumor and a medical report. It is single-use, highly specific, and designed to leave consequences that do not end with the cut. People who claim to have handled one rarely agree on where it came from, which is probably the point.

weapons.name: Fusion Blade
weapons.desc: The Fusion Blade is the sort of weapon you hear about from someone who swears they are not easily impressed. Armor becomes irrelevant with alarming speed and fights shorten accordingly. When it shows up, it tends to be in the hands of someone who does not explain themselves.

weapons.name: Fusion Lance
weapons.desc: The Fusion Lance takes that same principle and adds reach. It exists for targets that believed distance would buy them safety. The lesson is immediate and usually permanent.

weapons.name: Throwing knife
weapons.desc: The Throwing Knife is quiet, legal, and always present. It travels easily, leaves little behind, and rewards repetition rather than improvisation. People who rely on it tend to carry several and remember exactly where each one went.

weapons.name: Shuriken
weapons.desc: Shuriken favor preparation over force. Light, silent, and easily concealed, they trade individual impact for certainty through repetition. Their continued legality is widely attributed to the fact that no committee has ever agreed on how many constitute a weapon.

weapons.name: Chakram
weapons.desc: The Chakram looks ceremonial until it is in motion. Legal in most places and devastating in practiced hands, it rewards timing and followthrough rather than strength. Enthusiasts insist the return trajectory is the hardest part. Medical reports suggest the release was.

weapons.name: Blowgun
weapons.desc: The Blowgun is disciplined and patient. It operates without noise, without spectacle, and without urgency. Mastery takes time, and the results arrive quietly enough that most people never realize how much time was invested until someone stops breathing nearby.

weapons.name: Throwing axe
weapons.desc: The Throwing Axe became illegal after the Ishtar riots demonstrated that a few minor grip modifications were enough to turn a common tool into a reliable answer for armored security forces. The resulting ban did little to reduce enthusiasm and greatly increased creativity among tool manufacturers.

weapons.name: Composite Bow
weapons.desc: The Composite Bow persists because it is quiet, durable, and works without infrastructure or permission. Its ban followed the awkward realization that an unregulated sporting implement was outperforming licensed military weapons. The law fixed the security problem while conveniently turning a generation of hobbyists into criminals.

weapons.name: Crossbow
weapons.desc: The Crossbow was banned across the Alliance after Nerulian forces developed an unfortunate fondness for poisoned ammunition. The blanket prohibition was easier than rewriting doctrine and considerably less popular among hunters and hobbyists, who still insist the problem was chemistry, not engineering.

weapons.name: Hakari Greatbow
weapons.desc: The Hakari Greatbow reflects its culture openly. Powerful, demanding, and shaped by generations rather than manuals, it rewards discipline that cannot be rushed. Offworld observers often question the practicality of bow use by a species that prefers quadrupedal movement. Hakari instructors consider this an educational opportunity.
